metadata.purpose: semantic dependency and modifier-dominance layer for Chart 04 planning

claim_support.claim: Modern hub naming is often modifier-defined: the X before hub determines the object or domain.
claim_support.caution: This supports naming behavior, not every speaker's interpretation.

claim_support.claim: Hub is stable as a format but unstable as a single object category.
evidence_basis: 17 object types across retained hub forms
claim_support.caution: Object-type diversity comes from curated terms and source metadata, not a full language census.

claim_support.claim: Brand/platform forms show hub as a naming material rather than ordinary lexical frequency.
claim_support.caution: Brand recognition must not be equated with lexical frequency or semantic dominance.

claim_support.claim: The narrative can frame hub as semantically bleached only cautiously.
claim_support.caution: Use 'relational / underspecified / naming operator' rather than 'meaningless' or 'disappeared'.

claim_support.claim: The data cannot prove that many people first know hub through one brand example such as Pornhub.
evidence_basis: No audience-recognition survey in the dataset
claim_support.caution: Pornhub can be a neutral recognition anchor if used sparingly, but not proof of general cognition.

recommended_chart04_focus: Show hub as a center-word whose object is increasingly supplied by its modifier: X carries the domain, hub supplies the access/centrality format.
